headline: US stocks ended mixed as oil fell on US-Iran de-escalation and sharp chip weakness drove rotation into value and cyclicals ahead of Fed meeting and GDP data
raw_text:
- Major indices closed mixed with the Dow (DIA) leading gains and the Nasdaq (QQQ) slipping, as the S&P 500 (SPY) narrowly ended a recent losing streak and the Russell 2000 (IWM) outperformed
- Apple (AAPL) outperformed with a roughly 1% gain and reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company from Nvidia (NVDA), lifting the Dow (DIA)
- Oil (@CL) prices fell sharply on perceived US-Iran geopolitical de-escalation and a pause in hostilities, easing supply concerns and pressuring energy stocks
- Lower oil prices supported bonds and boosted airlines, travel, and other non-tech cyclical groups as investors rotated out of prior technology leaders
- Sector performance was broadly positive with 10 of 11 S&P groups higher, led by consumer defensive, communication services, real estate, and materials, while technology and energy lagged
- Real estate and materials notably outperformed, while the PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped more than 2% amid continued selling in chip names
- Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) each fell around mid-single digits, extending a three-day slide in semiconductor stocks amid rotation away from the Magnificent 7
- SanDisk (SNDK) sank by double digits on memory weakness tied to the blockbuster Shanghai IPO of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT, which also weighed on Micron (MU)
- No major after-hours earnings reactions were reported, with attention shifting to upcoming Big Tech results, this week’s Federal Reserve meeting, and GDP data
